plan: This is a second-price auction with 3 bidders and independent private values from $0-$49. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) when you win, bidding your value ensures you win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and avoid losses. Bidding higher than value risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $26.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $18, I should bid exactly $18 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values uniform on [0,49]. The dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid exactly my true value, since I pay the second-highest bid regardless of my own bid (as long as I win). Bidding my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and avoid losses. No information from previous rounds changes this optimal strategy. Therefore, I will bid $21, my true value.
